notes.title: Update Notes For July 8
notes.notes:
NOTE:  If the recent update causes you any problem, you can right-click the link in the Steam library, select Properties, go to the Betas tab, and choose a legacy version to revert to the previous version.

1. After clicking GO, you can now use in-model voice commands without system activation. This allows you to control game output with The Link’s voice commands even when playing with keyboard&mouse. (When you're tired, sit down and let The Link's voice commands continue helping you in-game. Just make sure your environment isn’t too noisy.)

2. "Geek Settings" has been renamed to "Advanced Settings", with more new options coming soon.

3. Controller mode has been removed (controller output will be integrated into the brand-new output system in next month's update). A new Privacy Mode has been added.

4. When Privacy Mode is enabled, you can automatically blur your face or completely hide the room environment and yourself during motion gaming. This makes it easier to record videos or stream motion gaming anytime, anywhere.

5. You can now convert a regular model to a privacy model with one click (automatically saved as a separate model), making it easier to share different game models with others online.(You might need to recapture failed to convert photos)

6. When operating a model that has been converted to Privacy Mode, all thumbnail images will default to privacy mode.

7. Improved display effect after selecting “Show Key Bindings”; the "???" issue no longer occurs.

8. You can now drag pages  in the main window just like dragging links

9. Optimized the pose model training algorithm, significantly improving the speed of training to “Capture” a pose.

10. The unique feature of The Link swapping left and right Ctrl keys by default is now clearly shown during mouse and keyboard recording (to avoid accidental  interact with the floating window).

11. Toggling the humanoid outline now automatically resets the floating window transparency to an appropriate%. Note: transparency only appear after system activation.

12. Fixed a bug where switching directly to simple mouse mode was not possible under Ultra Recognition Mode.

13.Improved Human Shape outline: when the outline is enabled, its transparency and brightness now match the appearance when the outline is disabled.

14. Fixed an issue where long page names could partially cover the settings and help buttons.

notes.title: Update Notes For June 14th
notes.notes: [p]NOTE:  If the recent update causes you any problem, you can right-click the link in the Steam library, select Properties, go to the Betas tab, and choose a legacy version to revert to the previous version.[/p][p](If you were already using the legacy version or you haven't used the link for a while, please note: the upper limit of jump sensitivity has been increased to 60. The Link now supports 4 performance modes.[/p][p]The previous “Quality Mode” and “Performance Mode” are now renamed to Quality and Standard modes.[/p][p]Two new modes have been added: Fast Mode and Lite Mode.[/p][p](In testing, even laptops under 200 dollar can run The Link smoothly in Lite Mode.)[/p][p]⚠️ Note: In Lite Mode, the frame rate is capped at 30 FPS, and The Link visibly reduces image clarity.[/p][p]As a result, Simple Mouse and Ultra Recognition may become nearly unusable.[/p][p]It is recommended to use a controller or custom pose + touch frames instead of gesture clicks.[/p][p]Also note: Different performance modes may require you to re-tune your Links.[/p][p]Once you've confirmed that your PC can run one mode smoothly with high FPS and no delay, try to avoid switching modes frequently.[/p][p]3. Floating window default size is now saved with global settings, not per model.[/p][p]5. from disabled pages will no longer be visible, even if set to “Show.”[/p][p]6. notes.title: Update Notes For May 12th
notes.notes:
NOTE:  If the recent update causes you any problem, you can right-click the link in the Steam library, select Properties, go to the Betas tab, and choose a legacy version to revert to the previous version.

1. Improved holding key trigger logic in action games (ACT).

2. For pose, when adjusting the "upper trigger sensitivity," the "lower exit sensitivity" will now change by maintaining the same difference.

3. In the system voice settings, you can now lift both hands for a moment to pause motion capture and can  reactivated at any time.

4. No longer required to add English (United States) for English speech recognition if you have another version of English installed.

5. You can now try using Windows Speech Recognition training to improve The Link's speech recognition performance.

6. Native support for rotating the camera 90 degrees left and right has been added to the beta version of The Link, allowing you to use your camera vertically. Notice: I’ve done my best to ensure that all previously recorded poses and hitboxes automatically adapt to the rotation, but you may need to redraw some hitbox if you rotated your camera.

7. Added two mini online game in Browse Models with True Jump and True Squat for Reference.

notes.title: Update Notes For April 21th
notes.notes:
1.Fixed a bug where creating a new model with a vertical resolution would cause the **hitbox positions to become misaligned.

2. The human outline will now always be displayed to help you draw the hitbox. The saved thumbnail will be clean, showing only you and the hitbox, without the outline.

notes.title: Update Notes For April 18th
notes.notes:
1. You can now double-click to edit the hitbox and drag to resize it directly, without having to redraw it each time.  
2. Fixed an bug where the original exit similarity would be lost after re-capture a pose.  
3. Fixed a bug where loading the model before the camera successfully started could cause the software to crash.

notes.title: Update notes for April 15
notes.notes:
1. Made minor improvements to the core detection and tracking algorithm.

2. Favorites can now be categorized — drag and organize them just like Links.

3. Multiple inputs can now be dragged to rearrange execution order.

4. Show Player Position updated:  
   - You can now optionally enable a floating window showing a player outline.  
   - Aligning yourself with this outline (camera positioned at your knee height) is recommended by MasonX as the standard setup.  
   - Most downloadable models will be designed based on this alignment in the future.

5. Touch boxes now auto-adapt:  
   - Touch boxes created in different resolutions or screen orientations (landscape or portrait) will now consistently stay aligned to the intended trigger area relative to the player.

6. Mirror Mode has been improved to auto-adapt to image transformations from most camera software, so you no longer need to disable it manually to avoid conflict.

7. Fixed a bug that could cause crashes when using Ultra Recognition Mode (tracking body and hand gestures simultaneously).

8. UI display optimized for different monitor resolutions, including 2K, 4K, and ultrawide screens.

9. Optimized Link display:  
   - The main interface now shows only small thumbnails and link names, making it easier to quickly locate needed links.  
   - Special controls are displayed as small icons next to the link name.

10. Each hitbox can now be set to appear or not in the floating window.  
   - When enabled, relevant hitboxes will display on the running window to help you trigger or avoid them more precisely.

11. Fixed a bug where mouse selection would jump to the opposite border when editing hitboxes.

12. Hardware recommendations section updated.

notes.title: The Link Update Note March 22
notes.notes:
Changed the Scroll Wheel Pose in Simple Mouse Mode so it won't interfere with the left and right click

NOTE:  If the recent update causes you any problem, you can right-click the link in the Steam library, select Properties, go to the Betas tab, and choose a legacy version to revert to the previous version.

notes.title: Update Notes – March 21st
notes.notes:
1 .Settings Integration:
All voice-related settings have been moved to System Voice Settings.
A new independent button for Motion Capture Window Settings has been added.

2. Display Player Positioning Feature:
By opening the Motion Capture Window Settings, you will now see a "Show Player Position" option.
This feature allows you to store a standing Position, making it easier to return to the original position while gaming.
Once show player position activated, the player’s position will also be displayed in the Hitbox Setup window to help you place your hitbox

3. Ultra Recognition Mode:
Ultra Recognition Mode is now available!
When activated, this feature allows you to track both custom hand gestures and full-body movements at the same time.
Currently, the enable/on/off switch is located under Wrist to Mouse Output. 

4. Tracking Options and Default Similarity Optimization:
The default tracking option for pose recognition is now set to both hands, and leg tracking will toggle on or off simultaneously.
After saving data, the system will now generate a default similarity value as a reference, depending on the tracking options you choose.

5. Quick Dropdown Menu:
Now, when you hover over "Add Pose" or "Switch Output", a dropdown menu will automatically appear, allowing for quicker and easier addition or editing of inputs and outputs.

6. Default Name When Adding to Favorites:
When adding a link to Favorites, the name input box in the pop-up window will now be pre-filled with the current link's name for convenience.

7. Fixed a bug where dragging a link with the mouse would make it excessively long and could mistakenly disable the link.

8. Wheel scroll gesture have been added to Simple Mouse Mode

9. Other Small Bug Fixes:

NOTE:  If the recent update causes you any problem, you can right-click the link in the Steam library, select Properties, go to the Betas tab, and choose a legacy version to revert to the previous version.

notes.title: Update Notes For March 1st
notes.notes:
1. The geek settings mode is now officially available. Currently, there is only one option: an algorithm that adjusts the impact of significant upper body movements on walking. Players who experience sudden stops in camera control or accidental walking triggers due to large upper body movements can try adjusting this algorithm.

2. Fixed an issue where a key conflict could potentially cause problems with unwanted key release.

3. The default orders of the saved link's outputs has been optimized to better align with  intuition, making it more convenient for users to change keybinds.

4. After considering some feedback, add walking recognition has been restored as a default- adding a constrain pose and a walking unit, consistent with the tutorial.

5. Fixed a bug that could cause The Link to crash directly when launched without any camera connected.

6. Fixed a bug that could result in multiple selection windows opening simultaneously when repeatedly clicking to add gesture recognition.

7. Added mouse relative movement duration control to the keyboard&mouse section (0.01~1s).

8. Increased the default similarity for the system off voice command.

9,  Made the system off pose easier to trigger.

10. Updated some UI descriptions and colors.

NOTE:  If the recent update causes you any problem, you can right-click the link in the Steam library, select Properties, go to the Betas tab, and choose a legacy version to revert to the previous version.

notes.title: The Link Update Notes — February 16
notes.notes:
1. Fixed an issue where the head tracking point still show under certain conditions(Head still tracking just hide the tracking point from display).

2 . Resolved a problem where HID drivers could fail to install correctly in specific scenarios.

3. Uninstalling and reinstalling the software now restores it to its initial first-time setup state. (Previously, Steam's default uninstallation process retained many data files.)

4. Updated certain text descriptions and instructions.

notes.title: The Link Update Notes For Feb 2
notes.notes:
1. Fixed some minor bugs.
2. All system voices are now saved globally by default; system activate and system off are no longer saved separately for different models.

Note: If the update causes issues with the software’s operation, you can always right-click, go to Properties → Betas, and select “legacy” to revert to the previous version.

notes.title: The Link Update Note For Jan 27
notes.notes:
1. Fixed some bugs with the simple mouse mode when adjusting the Real Hand Area.
2. The performance bar in the settings has been completely redone. You can now choose between Quality Mode or Performance Mode. After switching to Performance Mode and restarting, you’ll see a noticeable increase in frame rate.
3. Optimized some explanatory text in the Phone cam panel

notes.title: The Link Update Notes For Jan 25
notes.notes:
1. The Browse Models feature is now alive. You can watch demo videos and download templates for various games. Currently, demo videos have not been updated but will continue to add new game templates in the future.
2. The "Press Again" output logic can now be set with different keys for repeated execution (previously, it defaulted to the same key). Links previously set for "Press Again" need to be reopened and saved again (e.g., opening the map in World of Warcraft).
3. The hand recognition algorithm in the simple mouse mode has been optimized, improving the left and right mouse click efficiency in this mode.
4. Walk recognition now defaults to adding only one input unit.
5. All system control commands can now be set for auto-activation triggers. Voice recognition is no longer mandatory.
6. There is now an option to display keys triggered, allowing you to see which keys were triggered by the software in the running window (Press the small camera button to see this option).
7. Optimized the effect of the "Spam" mode. Now you can use it to achieve effects like keeping mouse moves in one direction with one pose (mostly used for camera control).
8. Save data can now be triggered without detecting a human body in the camera image.
9. When you open a link with keyboard outputs, the keyboard output panel will always be the default showing output.
10. Fixed a bug that could cause freezing when exiting directly from simple mouse mode.
11. A new viewing option has been added to the system voice settings.
12. To prevent accidental interaction with The Link operation window while holding down the Ctrl key in games, the default left and right Ctrl keys have been swapped.
13. Fixed a bug where turning system off with "raise both hands" as a system command could cause the software to automatically exit upon startup.
14. The tracking point on your head  is now hiding by default (actual tracking remains unaffected), allowing players to show their handsome faces.
15. Fixed a bug that  the " mirror mode" option can not be saved. Some cameras with inherent rotation or mirroring might cause issues in mirror mode, such as inability to draw frames or other bugs. In such cases, it is recommended to disable mirror mode (with the little camera button).
16. The color of disabled links is now red.
17. The button for loading models has been modified to distinguish between downloading and loading models.
18. Small link iamges can now better display voice commands.
19. The mobile app for The Link has officially entered the development phase. In the future, it will allow direct connection between the computer and the phone as a camera and microphone, as well as model import and adjustment directly on the phone, making it possible to use the software immediately upon download. For now, third-party tools like iVCam and DroidCam can be used as alternatives to use your phone as a camera and microphone for The Link.
NOTE:  If the recent update causes you any problem, you can right-click the link in the Steam library, select Properties, go to the Betas tab, and choose a legacy version to revert to the previous version.

notes.title: Update Notes For Jan 4
notes.notes:
Fixed a bug that could cause the speech recognition engine open multiple times and cause the camera to freeze or test voice not responding

Note: If the recent update causes you any problem, you can right-click the link in steam lib, select Properties, go to the Betas tab, and choose a legacy version to revert to the previous version.

notes.title: The Link Update notes Dec 30th
notes.notes:
1. Fixed an issue where the software UI size was shrinked when displayed on high-resolution monitors.
2. You can now click the small camera icon to adjust the transparency of the motion capture running window (automatically saved).
3. Fixed a bug where deleting an intermediate page and then creating a new one would cause the new page to be uncontrollable by the page control output.
4. Resolved freezing issues under certain conditions.
5. Added some tips and made other minor adjustments.

Note: If the update causes you any problem, you can right-click the link in steam lib, select Properties, go to the Betas tab, and choose a legacy version to revert to the previous version.

notes.title: The Link Update Notes For Dec 16
notes.notes:
1. Resolved an issue where mouse side buttons with certain drivers could not be triggered.
2. Reduced the chance of large movements being mistakenly identified as walking.
3. Optimized underlying algorithms and improved overall performance (your model may require slight 
  adjustments if your running FPS increases).
4. Fixed a bug where the frame rate might not display when running in non-mirror mode.
5. If the recent update causes any issues, you can always switch back to the Legacy version.

notes.title: The Link: Update notes For Dec 12
notes.notes:
1. Fixed an issue where dragging links on the main interface resulted in overly sensitive position changes.
2. Now, when a link is triggered by another link, a small image will display the name of the triggering link and automatically attach a holding-arrow icon.
3. Added a preset configuration model for Masonx Street Fighter 6 (Chinese version only).
4 .Fixed an issue where renaming a link and immediately clicking save wouldn’t save the name (previously, you had to press Enter to end the input).
5. Added explanations and fixed some error messages that were missing Chinese-language information.
